short: A crucial Yorkist victory where Edward IV defeated and killed his former ally, Richard Neville, Earl of Warwick.
full:
Fought in thick fog just north of London on 14 April 1471, the Battle of Barnet pitted Edward IV against a Lancastrian army led by Warwick the Kingmaker. The poor visibility caused confusion on the battlefield, leading to Lancastrian forces mistakenly attacking their own allies.

The resulting panic broke the Lancastrian line. Warwick was killed while attempting to reach his horse and flee, stripping the Lancastrian cause of its most powerful military and political backer. The victory paved the way for Edward IV to finally extinguish Lancastrian resistance weeks later.
